notes: Base A (more of the page's descriptive wording encoded). Final adds B's Clouded consciousness and Finding of tendency to bleed alongside A's forms, B's Recent qualifier on Drinking binge, and B's Venous stasis (finding) diagnosis. Diagnosis rule descriptions use B's '(changes in skin colour)' suffix for book-wide uniqueness; the task description is A's. Neither build encodes the descriptions under lower legs (red-brown discolouration, ulcers, spidery veins) or face (flat brown patches on cheeks, forehead, upper lip), so venous stasis and melasma rest on site alone while albinism and tinea versicolor require their descriptions; a clinician should judge that asymmetry (see the two unsettled questions). The is-a pairs (Acute confusion/Clouded consciousness; Bleeds easily/Finding of tendency to bleed) and same-concept pairs were each resolved once per role; the diff counts them both as only-A and only-B entries.
